newsitem.title: USA: Orange & Rockland offers restructuring proposals.
newsitem.headline: Orange & Rockland offers restructuring proposals.

text.p: Orange and Rockland Utilities Inc said Tuesday it is filing a multi-year plan to restructure company operations with the New York State Public Service Commission.
The plan seeks to expand the utility's PowerPick energy supply choice program. In addition, it proposes power generation would be functionally separated in 1997.
The proposal commits the company to freeze "its current electric rates through nearly the end of the century, and perhaps beyond," the company said without explanation in its statement.
Over the past 16 months, Orange & Rockland noted, it has reduced New York electric rates 6.4 percent in three cuts.

Chief executive officer D. Louis Peoples said, "Today's filing introduces innovative, yet practical and effective, proposals to create a fully competitive marketplace for electric energy and services.
The filing was made on the deadline established by the Public Service Commission in May.
The utility said it proposes to implement a Competitive Transition Charge to provide a reasonable opportunity to recover its stranded generation costs.

It said this would be a fixed, mandatory customer charge that would be in effect for eight years. At the end of the period, the charge would be rescinded, and the utility would then be required to absorb whatever stranded costs had not been fully recovered.
This proposal would not increase prices because rates are now based on cost levels that cover the costs that would be stranded when competition is introduced, the company noted.
Orange & Rockland has also moved to cut its stranded costs by selling the facilities to customers who want to use them in a deregulated market.

On the consent agenda for Wednesday's Public Service Commission meeting in New York City is a proposal to sell substation equipment to American Home Products Corp's Lederle division, a participant in the utility's PowerPick pilot.
The utility said its filing also ...

...endorses creation of an Independent System Operator to administer a wholesale electric energy commodity market for wholesale competition at the earliest possible date consistent with maintaining system reliability.

...proposes expanding PowerPick's energy-supply choice to all customers 12 months after the implementation of wholesale competition, and to offer choice of energy supplier and capacity to all its customers three years after wholesale's implementation.
...seeks customer service performance standards for all competitors. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710
